inventory_panel.basis: 24 SKUs, 20,000 simulated lead times. Demand shares a common factor with pairwise log-demand correlation 0.48 (measured from 12 shared periods). The independent figures are what the engine reported before and are kept beside these so the difference is visible.

Refund per month rose from $0.00 to $996.84 since 2026-05-01; that is $996.84 more per month
sales per click rose from $3.27 to $3.43 since 2026-01-21; at 52 clicks a day that is $240.59 of attributed sales over 30 days
1 spend spike(s) in the last 14 days; largest on 2026-08-19: $184.10 against an expected $124.63 for that weekday (robust z +3.5); spend above expectation on those days totals $59.47
fee per unit fell from $9.00 to $8.73 since 2026-02-01

assumptions: A sale becomes payable 10 days after it is made (delivery assumed 2 days, then Amazon's reserve until 7 days after delivery, DD+7); Amazon settles every 14 days and the transfer is assumed to reach your bank 4 days later (3 business days; Amazon says up to 5). Your settlement date is not on file, so the last transfer is assumed to have reached your bank today and the next to land in 14 days, the longest wait

The platform already holds your last 14 days of sales, not part of your stated cash: about $95,997 net of fees, drawn from the same demand model as the days ahead (your payments page shows the real balance); the first transfers pay it
Ad spend leaves your cash the day it is spent; where the platform takes it out of a later payout instead, your balance in between runs a little higher than shown
Demand rate is flat over the horizon (no seasonal estimate on file)
Fixed costs accrue daily (monthly / 30); real due dates may be lumpier
Cash on hand and monthly fixed costs are client-stated, not modeled
Demand generator identical to the inventory simulation (lognormal rate, Poisson counts)
Demand shares a common factor across SKUs: pairwise log-demand correlation 0.4805, measured from this catalog's own history
The trough is reported with its expected shortfall (the mean of the worst 5% of troughs), not only its 5th percentile

assumptions: Demand per SKU: daily rate ~ lognormal matched to (point, sd), units ~ Poisson(rate × days) — the same generator as the inventory simulation and cash-flow cone
Demand shares a common factor across SKUs: pairwise log-demand correlation 0.4805, measured from this catalog's own history. Independent draws would put the tail far closer to the mean than it is.
Unit contribution (revenue − Amazon fees − COGS) / units and ad spend are frozen at the latest period (2026-08-01 to 2026-08-31); only unit volume is uncertain
Loss = expected net − simulated net; VaR/CVaR are dollars below expectation, not absolute losses
24 SKU(s) use the forecast model's daily rate and error sd
